## Proof

Let $K_\mathfrak{p}$ denote the completion of $K$ at the finite prime $\mathfrak{p}$, with $\mathfrak{p} \mid p$. Then $K_\mathfrak{p}$ is a finite extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$; write $e$ for the ramification index, $f$ for the residue degree, and $q = p^f$ for the cardinality of the residue field $\mathbb{F}_q = \mathcal{O}_\mathfrak{p}/\mathfrak{p}$. Let $d = [K_\mathfrak{p} : \mathbb{Q}_p] = ef \geq 1$.

### Step 1. Structure of the local unit group

The unit group of the ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_\mathfrak{p}$ decomposes as

$$\mathcal{O}_\mathfrak{p}^{\times} \cong \mu_{q-1} \times (1 + \mathfrak{p}),$$

where $\mu_{q-1}$ is the group of $(q-1)$-th roots of unity (the Teichmüller lift of $\mathbb{F}_q^{\times}$) and $1 + \mathfrak{p}$ is the group of principal units. This is the standard decomposition coming from Hensel's lemma: every unit has a unique Teichmüller representative times a principal unit.

### Step 2. The $p$-completion of $\mu_{q-1}$ is trivial

Since $q = p^f$, we have $\gcd(q-1, p) = 1$. Thus $\mu_{q-1}$ is a finite group of order $q - 1$, which is coprime to $p$. The $p$-completion (pro-$p$ completion) of a finite group of order coprime to $p$ is trivial, because there are no normal subgroups of $p$-power index. Equivalently, $\varprojlim \mu_{q-1}/\mu_{q-1}^{p^n} = \{1\}$ since the $p$-th power map is an automorphism of $\mu_{q-1}$.

### Step 3. $1 + \mathfrak{p}$ is already a pro-$p$ group

The principal unit group admits the filtration

$$1 + \mathfrak{p} \supset 1 + \mathfrak{p}^2 \supset 1 + \mathfrak{p}^3 \supset \cdots$$

with $1 + \mathfrak{p} = \varprojlim_n (1+\mathfrak{p})/(1+\mathfrak{p}^n)$. Each successive quotient satisfies

$$(1 + \mathfrak{p}^n)/(1 + \mathfrak{p}^{n+1}) \cong \mathbb{F}_q^+ \cong (\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^f,$$

so the order of $(1+\mathfrak{p})/(1+\mathfrak{p}^n)$ is $q^{n-1} = p^{f(n-1)}$, a power of $p$. Hence each finite quotient is a $p$-group, and $1 + \mathfrak{p}$ is a pro-$p$ group. A pro-$p$ group is equal to its own pro-$p$ completion, so the $p$-completion of $1 + \mathfrak{p}$ is $1 + \mathfrak{p}$ itself.

### Step 4. $1 + \mathfrak{p}$ is infinite

The $p$-adic logarithm $\log : 1 + \mathfrak{p}^n \to \mathfrak{p}^n$ is an isomorphism of $\mathbb{Z}_p$-modules for all $n > e/(p-1)$ (for $p$ odd; for $p = 2$ one takes $n$ sufficiently large as well). Since $\mathfrak{p}^n \cong \mathcal{O}_\mathfrak{p} \cong \mathbb{Z}_p^d$ as a $\mathbb{Z}_p$-module, the subgroup $1 + \mathfrak{p}^n$ is isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}_p^d$ with $d = [K_\mathfrak{p}:\mathbb{Q}_p] \geq 1$.

The quotient $(1+\mathfrak{p})/(1+\mathfrak{p}^n)$ is finite, so $1 + \mathfrak{p}$ is a finite extension (as a $\mathbb{Z}_p$-module) of $\mathbb{Z}_p^d$. In particular, $1 + \mathfrak{p}$ is a finitely generated $\mathbb{Z}_p$-module of $\mathbb{Z}_p$-rank $d \geq 1$, hence is uncountably infinite. (Concretely, $1 + \mathfrak{p}$ contains the uncountable subgroup $1 + \mathfrak{p}^n \cong \mathbb{Z}_p^d$.)

### Step 5. Conclusion

The $p$-completion of $\mathcal{O}_\mathfrak{p}^{\times}$ is

$$\widehat{(\mathcal{O}_\mathfrak{p}^{\times})}_p \;\cong\; \widehat{(\mu_{q-1})}_p \times \widehat{(1+\mathfrak{p})}_p \;=\; \{1\} \times (1+\mathfrak{p}) \;\cong\; 1 + \mathfrak{p},$$

which is infinite (indeed uncountable, being a $\mathbb{Z}_p$-module of rank $[K_\mathfrak{p}:\mathbb{Q}_p] \geq 1$).

**The $p$-completion of the unit group $\mathcal{O}_\mathfrak{p}^{\times}$ is infinite.** $\blacksquare$
